Hi,

 I am new to lavaan, but am finding it to a very useful tool to conduct sem.

 I am running a second order model ( a very simple one) as below:

#21 item scale
#4 factor model (all)
FHS1<-list(NA)
FHS1<-read.csv("U:\\harmony\\for cfa only 21 items (paper24) r.csv", header=TRUE)
fhs1.cov<-cov(FHS1)

FHS.model <- '# LATENT VARIABLE DEFINITIONS
         com =~ P8 + P9 + P13 + P10 + P16 + P20
         con =~ P17 + P19 + P21 + P23
         qua =~ P1 + P5 + P6 + P7 + P18 + P22 + P24
         fore =~ P11 + P12 + P14 + P15
         
         # BETA (CAUSAL PATHS)
         har =~ com + con + qua + fore
'
fit<-cfa(FHS.model, data=FHS1, std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLM", test = "satorra.bentler", meanstructure=TRUE)
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

The above model runs well. however when I try to constrain factor loadins and use the below syntax:

fit1<-cfa(FHS.model, data=FHS1, std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLM", test = "satorra.bentler", group="sex", group.equal=c("loadings"))

messages.subject: Re: constraining factor loadings of first order factors in a higher order model
parts:
Or am
> I reading it wrong/doing something wrong?

I think you are reading the output wrong, because as far as I can see,
the factor loadings in your output (see 'Estimate' column) are identical
in both groups. Both for first and second order factors.

Yves.
